entries.title: More Photos Released by Oversight Dems Give Disturbing Glimpse Into Epstein’s World
entries.summary: The photos are just the latest obtained and released by Democrats on the House Oversight Committee.
entries.content:
Democrats on the House Oversight Committee released on Thursday nearly 70 photos that were obtained from the Jeffrey Epstein estate, including a screenshot of a message stating a friend “sent me some girls today. But she asks 1000$ per girl.” The message lists the height and weight of an 18-year-old woman. “Maybe someone will be good for J?”

The images offer more disturbing glimpses of the life of the late convicted sex offender and disgraced financier. The release also includes a photo of a handwritten passage of Vladimir Nabokov’s “Lolita” on what appears to be a woman’s foot, a photo of a censored Ukrainian woman’s passport, a photo of Bill Gates with a woman whose face is censored and a photo of Noam Chomsky with Epstein on a plane.

Democrats say they did not obtain any context on the photos from the Epstein estate and that they are presented as they were received. This is the latest release from Democrats since they obtained 95,000 photos from Epstein’s estate.
entries.author: Daniella Diaz

entries.title: Senate Republicans Throw Cold Water on ACA Subsidy Discharge Petition
entries.summary: “It could pass the House, right?” Republican Sen. John Hoeven said. “But for it to pass the Senate, we're going to have some reforms.”
entries.content:
Democratic members of the House were elated that enough Republicans joined them in signing a discharge petition to force a vote on a three-year extension of expiring Affordable Care Act subsidies. But in the Senate, members are hemming and hawing about whether they’d take the bill up at all.

Right now, signs point to no.

“I don’t think a three-straight, three-year extension will pass,” Sen. John Hoeven, a Republican from North Dakota, told NOTUS. “We’ve got to have reforms. It could pass the House, right? But for it to pass the Senate, we’re going to have some reforms.”
entries.author: Avani Kalra, Ursula Perano
